questions.q: Where did David assemble the leaders of Israel?
questions.a: David assembled them in Jerusalem.

questions.q: What did David say he wanted to build?
questions.a: David said he wanted to build a temple as a resting place for the ark of the covenant of Yahweh.

questions.q: Why did God say David could not build a temple for his name?
questions.a: God said that he could not build it because he was a man of war and had shed blood.

questions.q: Whom did Yahweh choose to be king over all of Israel?
questions.a: Yahweh chose David to be king over all of Israel.

questions.q: What did Yahweh choose Solomon, David’s son, to do over Israel?
questions.a: He chose Solomon to sit on the throne of the kingdom of Yahweh, over Israel.

questions.q: According to Yahweh, what would Solomon build?
questions.a: Yahweh said that Solomon would build his house and his courts.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say he would do for Solomon if he remained committed to obey his commandments?
questions.a: Yahweh said that he would establish his kingdom forever.

questions.q: If all the people kept the commandments of Yahweh, what would happen to the good land they possessed?
questions.a: They would possess the good land and leave it as an inheritance to their children after them forever.

questions.q: What does Yahweh understand of everyone’s thoughts?
questions.a: He understands every motivation of everyone’s thoughts.

questions.q: What will happen if Solomon abandons Yahweh?
questions.a: Yahweh will reject him permanently.

questions.q: What did David tell Solomon about the word of Yahweh?
questions.a: David told Solomon that Yahweh chose him to build a temple as a sanctuary.

questions.q: What did David give to his son Solomon?
questions.a: David gave Solomon the plans for the temple, including its porch, rooms, and storerooms.

questions.q: What were the storerooms in God’s house and the treasuries to store?
questions.a: The storerooms and the treasuries were for the things consecrated for the temple.

questions.q: Where were the priests and Levites assigned responsibilities to serve?
questions.a: Their assigned responsibilities were for the service in the house of Yahweh.

questions.q: What did David tell Solomon about the gold and silver for the articles used in the temple service?
questions.a: David told him how much gold and silver to use for each article.

questions.q: What did David tell Solomon about the lampstands and lamps?
questions.a: David told him how much gold and silver to use for each lampstand and its lamps.

questions.q: What did David tell Solomon about the gold and silver tables?
questions.a: David told him how much gold and silver to use for the tables, including the table for the bread.

questions.q: What did David tell Solomon to make of pure gold?
questions.a: David told him to make the forks, basins, and pitchers of pure gold.

questions.q: What did David tell Solomon to make for covering the ark of the covenant?
questions.a: David told him to make gold cherubs that would spread their wings over the ark of the covenant of Yahweh.

questions.q: How was David directed in all the things he put in writing?
questions.a: Yahweh directed him and helped him understand the plan.

questions.q: What did David promise Solomon about Yahweh’s presence until all the work was finished?
questions.a: David told Solomom that Yahweh would not leave him nor abandon him until all the work for the service of Yahweh’s temple was finished.

questions.q: What were the leaders and all the people ready to do?
questions.a: They were ready to begin using their skills to help Solomon to build the house of God.

commentary.text: David exhorts the people to the fear of the Lord.
He gives instructions for the temple.

Verses 1–10 During David's last sickness, many chief priests and Levites were at Jerusalem. Finding himself able, David spoke of his purpose to build a temple for God, and of God's disallowing that purpose. He opened to them God's gracious purposes concerning Solomon. David charged them to cleave stedfastly to God and their duty. We cannot do our work as we should, unless we put on resolution, and fetch in strength from Divine grace. Religion or piety has two distinct parts. The first is knowledge of God, the second is worship of God. David says, Know thou the God of thy father, and serve him with a perfect heart and a willing mind. God is made known by his works and word. Revelation alone shows the whole character of God, in his providence, his holy law, his condemnation of sinners, his blessed gospel, and the ministration of the Spirit to all true believers. The natural man cannot receive this knowledge of God. But thus we learn the value of the Saviour's atonement, and of the sanctification of the Holy Spirit, and are influenced to walk in all his commandments. It brings a sinner to his proper place at the foot of the cross, as a poor, guilty, helpless worm, deserving wrath, yet expecting every thing needful from the free mercy and grace of God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ. Having been forgiven much, the pardoned sinner learns to love much.

The temple must be a sacred thing, and a type of Christ; it must be framed by Divine teaching. Christ is the true temple, the church is the gospel temple, and heaven the everlasting temple; all are framed according to the Divine counsels, and the plan laid in the Divine wisdom, ordained before the world, for God's glory and our good. David gave this pattern to Solomon, that he might go by rule. Materials were provided for the most costly utensils of the temple. Directions were given which way to look for help in this great undertaking. Be not dismayed; God will help thee, and thou must look up to him in the first place. We may be sure that God, who owned our fathers, and carried them through the services of their day, will, in like manner, never leave us, while he has any work to do in us, or by us. Good work is likely to go on, when all concerned are hearty in furthering it. Let us hope in God's mercy; if we seek him, he will be found of us.
